title: A broker outage permanently drops the initial review
claim: The facade publishes after the TaskRun transaction commits. _start_stamphog_review catches publish failures and only writes a log. No database record or scheduled sweep retries this handoff.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: The toggle gate checks one assignee instead of any assignee
claim: The resolver contract checks the selected acting reviewer only. The webhook gate treats None as a global opt-out. If the first assignee is off and a later assignee is on, no review runs, conflicting with the stated rule that any assigned user's opt-in enables Stamphog.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: A broker failure permanently drops the initial review
claim: The handler catches every broker publish failure after the TaskRun output commits and only writes a log. No durable record remains, Celery retries cannot run because the broker never accepted the task, so the PR misses its initial Stamphog review permanently.
validator_reason: "Never reviews again" overstated — later pushes and TaskRun saves re-fire with head-keyed dedupe, and Celery publish retries absorb blips. But the initial draft-time review can be lost with only a log during a sustained broker outage; same mode exists by design on the Temporal leg. Real but low probability, heavyweight remedy — downgraded to consider.

title: Carve-out failures block stale approval dismissal
claim: The exception path retries before the code reaches _retract_stale_approvals_on_skip. Celery drops the delivery after retries fail, so a previous approval can remain active after unreviewed commits; a partial database outage can cause this state.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: A worker crash can lose the initial review
claim: Celery uses early acknowledgement because this task does not set acks_late. A worker crash before row creation loses the initial review; a crash after commit can leave a queued run without a workflow.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Self-driving attribution misses failure paths
claim: The new property only reaches events emitted inside the sandbox. stamphog_review_failed omits it, and failures before sandbox creation produce only logs, so dashboards cannot compare failure rates for inbox vs normal reviews.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Child environments fail the team identity checks
claim: StamphogRepoConfig stores the canonical parent team ID while TaskRun stores the child environment ID; the facade rejects these raw IDs as unequal and this caller repeats that check, so later pushes from child environments lose the inbox carve-out and skip review.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: The carve-out trusts caller-controlled PR linkage
claim: Docs claim both trigger paths verify the PR-to-TaskRun link, but process_inbox_pr_review trusts supplied identifiers, and the webhook path accepts caller-writable TaskRun.output.pr_url; a caller can point a qualifying run at another accessible PR and bypass approval gates via the self-driving flag.
validator_reason: Dismissed: no attacker-reachable path — identifiers come from the resolver-gated receiver or HMAC-verified webhook payloads, pr_url is server-written, team scope is re-verified in the facade, and only two gates are relaxed by documented design. Remaining kernel is defensive-coding guidance already in docstrings.

title: The toggle gate ignores other opted-in assignees
claim: The PR promises a review when any assigned reviewer enables the toggle, but this text documents a single acting reviewer; callers check only that user's toggle, so another assigned reviewer can enable it and still receive no initial or follow-up review.
validator_reason: Dismissed: single canonical acting reviewer is a documented maintainer decision (2026-07-02/03) — one person's settings govern each run to avoid nondeterminism. The review still runs when the acting reviewer opts in; at most a product-design discussion, not a defect this PR must fix.

title: Initial inbox review trusts caller-controlled provenance
claim: TaskRun.output.pr_url is caller-writable but the worker never loads task_run_id or signal_report_id; it only checks the team configured the URL's repository, trusts acting_user_id and the earlier toggle result, then stamps inbox_review, bypassing bot and draft gates — a task writer can target an unrelated open PR and cause a real approval.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Webhook carve-out uses writable fields as security evidence
claim: find_task_run treats TaskRun.output.pr_url and TaskRun.branch as proof a run produced the PR, but public TaskRun update routes let callers change both; a caller can point a linked run at an unrelated repo-native bot PR, and the next webhook marks it self-driving and skips bot, review-mode, and author-permission gates.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Only one reviewer controls the any-reviewer toggle
claim: _resolve_assigned_reviewer returns one user and both Stamphog paths check only that user's setting; if the first reviewer opted out and a later one opted in, the initial review does not run and a later webhook can dismiss the existing approval, conflicting with the any-assigned-reviewer requirement.
validator_reason: Confirmed: implementation checks exactly one reviewer against the PR's stated any-assignee gate; master already ships the fix (_pick_stamphog_reviewer selects any opted-in reviewer). Failure direction is conservative (suppressed reviews, never unreviewed approvals) and feature-flagged — downgraded to should_fix.

title: Qualification filters run after an unrelated row can win
claim: find_task_run selects one row before the facade checks team_id, signal_report_id, and internal; duplicate PR URLs and branches across teams or task types let an unrelated row win the selection, so the facade returns None even when a qualifying signal run exists.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Self-driving instructions conflict with the system prompt
claim: The system prompt says every bot author needs human review and treats the stamphog label as a confidence signal; this flow has a bot author and no label, and _format_self_driving() adds its exception only to the lower-priority user prompt, so the model can refuse every intended review or use a nonexistent confidence signal.
validator_reason: Dismissed: decisive premise false — the self-driving block lands in the TRUSTED context region, not the user prompt; both predicted failure modes are structurally prevented (self_driving waives bot-author and draft gates), and inbox PRs never get the stamphog label, so no confidence signal exists to misuse. Suggested change duplicates tested behavior.

title: Ready self-driving PRs are reported as drafts
claim: The prompt always says the PR is a draft, but a self-driving PR can become ready before a later push starts another review, so the trusted prompt reports false state for this supported path.
validator_reason: Confirmed: _format_self_driving emits the draft sentence unconditionally while PRData.draft holds the actual state; the ready_for_review + synchronize re-review path builds the trusted prompt with a false draft claim that can skew the verdict. Kept at should_fix — real correctness defect, not security or data loss.

title: A transient lookup error leaves the switch disabled until reload
claim: Every lookup error becomes a successful response with stamphog_connected false; the frontend treats false as confirmed missing connection, disables the switch, and the successful request never triggers failure retry, so the switch stays disabled after recovery until another settings request.
validator_reason: Mechanism confirmed: a product-DB blip yields false in a 200 so the retry banner never appears. But the degradation is deliberate and documented, fails safe (can only disable), self-heals on next scene mount, and affects an opt-in experiment surface — downgraded to consider.

title: Failed same-head reviews have no retry limit
claim: The dedupe excludes all FAILED runs and each later TaskRun output save queues the task again, so a deterministic failure can consume GitHub, Temporal, and LLM capacity without limit.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Opt-out skips the stale-approval fallback
claim: process_inbox_pr_review is the documented fallback for a lost synchronize webhook, but the receiver queues it only when the resolved reviewer has the toggle on; after an opt-out (or None resolution) a new head queues no Stamphog work, so an old approval stays active over unreviewed commits and can satisfy a required review.
validator_reason: Confirmed asymmetry: webhook path dismisses on opt-out but the fallback leg is toggle-gated, so head-keyed dismissal never fires. Requires a rare compound failure (lost webhook + opted-out reviewer) behind an experiment flag, and the suggested reconciliation job is heavyweight — downgraded to should_fix.

title: Connection status accepts an unusable credential owner
claim: has_reviewable_repo_config only checks connected_by_user_id is non-null; the plain cross-database integer survives user deletion or deactivation, so the settings API reports true and enables the switch while every review fails at _mint_reviewer_gateway_token, which requires an active user.
validator_reason: Confirmed divergence between the facade's null check and the mint-time active-user check; a deleted/deactivated connector yields an enabled switch with always-failing reviews. Self-heals on re-sync, fails closed, no security exposure. Kept at should_fix — real consistency gap with a concrete user-visible consequence, not merge-blocking.

title: The gate rejects the self-driving tasks it must identify
claim: Signals creates automatic implementation tasks with internal=True, and this new condition rejects every one of those tasks; the ReviewHog save receiver also rejects them, so the target self-driving PRs receive no initial review and no webhook re-review.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: An older completed run can hide the latest failed review
claim: The query removes FAILED and SUPERSEDED rows before selecting the newest run; a newer failed re-review can share a head with an older completed run, which then stops the retry path, leaving the current diff without a new verdict after a same-head reopen or base-retarget review fails.
validator_reason: No verdict recorded (did not reach/pass validation).

title: Self-driving retries get stranded on the current head
claim: This path has no stamphog label; the engine can still return WAIT, ERROR, or a migration gate result, which the hosted workflow stores as terminal runs. process_inbox_pr_review then treats that head as already reviewed and check-run completion does not restart, so a temporary delay prevents a completed review until another commit arrives.
validator_reason: Confirmed on every claim: transient outcomes persist as terminal GATED/FAILED runs, head-keyed dedupe restarts only QUEUED, so the head is never re-reviewed until a new commit. Defeats the feature's triage-time review guarantee. Kept at should_fix — real liveness defect, not security or data loss.
